title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Naval Drone Duel

### The Breakthrough
The Ukrainian Sargan‑3000 uncrewed surface vessel equipped with a 12.7 mm Kongsberg Protector remote weapon station engaged and sank the Russian Orcan USV, marking the first documented USV‑vs‑USV kill. This demonstrates that small, expendable surface drones can deliver lethal force against peer unmanned platforms.

### The Caveats
The claim rests on a single news report with no independent verification or quantitative data.

## mjbatch

### The Breakthrough
mjbatch introduces a GIL‑free C++ thread pool that can step up to 4 096 MuJoCo simulations in parallel, exposing live NumPy‑style views of simulation state. The library showed a Go1 quadruped learning to walk in under a minute on a five‑year‑old laptop, enabling fast reinforcement‑learning and co‑design without GPUs.

### The Caveats
No quantitative comparison to existing parallel MuJoCo frameworks is provided, leaving the speed advantage unverified.

## shodh-memory

### The Breakthrough
shodh-memory delivers deterministic, offline memory for AI agents and ROS2 robots using Rust‑based Hebbian strengthening, power‑law decay, and local MiniLM embeddings via ONNX, with reported storage latency of ~55 ms—orders of magnitude faster than cloud‑based alternatives.

### The Caveats
Latency figures are presented without any evaluation of retrieval accuracy or memory quality, so the effectiveness of the offline memory remains unproven.

## AutonomousKart

### The Breakthrough
The AutonomousKart repository offers a ROS2 package with colcon builds, launch files that switch between simulation and real‑world kart, and GitHub Actions CI, targeting a Raspberry Pi for on‑board execution—providing an open‑source stack for rapid autonomous‑vehicle prototyping.

### The Caveats
The repo supplies launch scripts but no real‑world performance metrics or baseline comparisons, so its effectiveness on actual hardware is unverified.

### Priority
The naval duel provides the clearest evidence that autonomous surface robots can now achieve lethal, peer‑to‑peer combat outcomes, making it the most concrete hardware milestone for today’s robotics scan.

### One action
Track independent verification of the Sargan‑3000 engagement and consider its remote‑weapon‑station integration when evaluating USV concepts.

### What to watch
Both mjbatch and shodh-memory are software tools that expand robot research capabilities: mjbatch scales simulation for learning and design, while shodh-memory aims to give agents fast, offline knowledge retrieval. Watching their adoption could signal broader trends toward CPU‑centric, low‑latency robotics pipelines.
